subject: Post-call: migration route options + config asks
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Jared Klein <jared.klein@finovo.com>, Priya George <priya.george@finovo.com>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Jun 2027 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: migration route options + config asks

Thanks again for taking the call this morning — quick recap and proposed next steps so we can scope a concrete migration plan. Notes below are high-level; happy to sketch timelines and a sample cost estimate once you confirm a few items.

Call highlights (what we heard)
- Current setup: self-hosted inference on legacy GPU cluster (8 x A100) behind an internal API gateway.
- Desired: lower latency, better cost per token, and simpler deployment model for engineering org.
- Constraints: data residency (must remain in your VPC), procurement prefers a monthly committed spend target.

Redwood options that fit your situation (short):
1) Hosted API: fastest to try — zero infra to manage, but data flows through Redwood-hosted endpoints (we can restrict region and encrypted in transit). Good for rapid proof-of-concept.
2) Dedicated capacity: reserved GPU pool in our infra for your org only — predictable throughput and easier on/off ramp from self-hosted; supports VPC peering for private traffic egress.
3) Private (VPC / on‑prem): customer-managed networking with our private control plane — best for strict compliance and full data isolation. Longer lead time and procurement steps.

Migration approaches we recommended:
- Lift-and-shift to Dedicated first (minimal code changes) -> enable VPC peering + private routing -> later migrate to Private if needed.
- Alternatively, Hybrid: split latency-sensitive calls to Dedicated and batch/async workloads to Hosted.

Open questions (please reply inline):
- Do you have a strict requirement that traffic not leave your VPC at any time, or is peered, encrypted routing acceptable for an initial POC?
- Current peak throughput (req/s) and average payload sizes (tokens per request)?
- Which models / formats are you running now (LLama 2/3, custom finetunes, tokenizer)?
- Procurement: is the $40k/month committed spend you mentioned a firm number or a target range?

Attachments: SOC2_attestation_v3.pdf (security attestation), MVP_Migration_steps.xlsx (starter migration checklist).

Proposed next steps:
- Tech workshop with infra + security (30–60m) to validate VPC peering and network reqs.
- Redwood to provide Dedicated trial sizing and cost estimate based on traffic numbers.
- Security questionnaire + SOC2 evidence exchange.

Suggested times for the workshop: Thu 6/3 10am PT or Fri 6/4 9am PT. If neither works, send some slots and we’ll accommodate.

Thanks —
Marcus Lin
Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0143

From: Jared Klein <jared.klein@finovo.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya George <priya.george@finovo.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Jun 2027 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: migration route options + config asks

Thanks Marcus — useful summary. A few clarifications inline: 

- Data residency: procurement and security prefer traffic and logs to remain in our AWS VPC; we may be able to accept VPC peering for an initial window (30–90 days) during the POC but long-term we want Private or on‑prem.
- Throughput: steady-state ~40 req/s, peak bursts ~150 req/s (in spikes). Average request size ~320 tokens in/120 tokens out.
- Models: currently running a mix — distilled Llama 2 variants and some internal finetunes (PyTorch). Tokenizer is sentencepiece-based.
- Procurement: $40k/mo is the upper target for committed spend; we can flex for an initial POC.

Hybrid question: yes — we want a hybrid option during migration so we can cutover critical endpoints early. Are there limitations on routing between Hosted and Dedicated in terms of context/caching or KV cache migration?

We can do Thu 6/3 10am PT for the workshop. Please include the networking and security folks on the invite.

- Jared
Head of ML Platforms | Finovo
jared.klein@finovo.com

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Jared Klein <jared.klein@finovo.com>, Priya George <priya.george@finovo.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 2 Jun 2027 09:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: migration route options + config asks

Great — thanks for the extra detail, Jared. Short answers: hybrid routing is supported, but there are considerations around KV cache portability and session affinity if you split a single user flow between Hosted and Dedicated. We’ll call these out in the workshop.

Proposed migration plan (high level):
- Phase 0 (Week 0–1): Security & network alignment (VPC peering feasibility) and model compatibility check (tokenizer + formats).
- Phase 1 (Week 2–4): Dedicated trial — mirror traffic (shadow mode) then cut a subset of low-risk endpoints.
- Phase 2 (Week 5–8): Full cutover for latency-critical endpoints; evaluate moving to Private if procurement/compliance require it.

What Redwood will bring to the workshop:
- Technical runbook for dedicated sizing and autoscaling policies (cost/latency tradeoffs).
- KV cache migration notes and recommended session-affinity patterns.
- SOC2 evidence and network peering checklist (see attached network_topology.png).

Next steps for the meeting on Thu 6/3 10am PT: please send calendar invites and attach network ACLs/allowed egress CIDR list if possible. I’ve added Neha (solutions engineering) and Soojin (infrastructure manager) to help scope the Dedicated sizing and security needs.

Attachments: network_topology.png, MVP_Migration_steps.xlsx

Looking forward —
Marcus Lin
Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Jared Klein <jared.klein@finovo.com>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>, Priya George <priya.george@finovo.com>
Date: Wed, 2 Jun 2027 11:00:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: migration route options + config asks

Quick internal note + checklist for the workshop (copying Finovo):

We’ll want the following artifacts before or during the workshop to produce an accurate Dedicated trial sizing and cost estimate: 
- Network: Allowed egress CIDRs, VPC peering contact, any proxy/firewall in front of your API, and whether mTLS is required.
- Traffic: representative 24h pcap or synthetic load numbers (req/s over time), and token histograms if available.
- Models: exact model names and sizes, whether you need custom finetunes to be hosted, and framework (Torch/TensorFlow/ONNX).
- Storage/Logs: retention window for request/response logs and whether logs can be stored in our encrypted bucket or must stay in your S3.

Operational asks: 
- Can Finovo share an internal contact for procurement to coordinate the trial commitment paperwork?
- Any hard SLA requirements (p99 latency target, availability SLA)?

We will prepare a short appendix on KV cache portability and session-affinity to present at the workshop. I’m available Thu 6/3 10am PT and will bring a template security questionnaire that we can use to accelerate the compliance exchange.

Neha Kapoor
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.com
